newsitem.title: BURKINA FASO: Burkina Faso scraps two-term limit on presidency.
newsitem.headline: Burkina Faso scraps two-term limit on presidency.

text.p: The Burkina Faso parliament has voted overwhelmingly to ditch constitutional provisions limiting the presidential mandate to two seven-year terms.
The opposition denounced the approval of the bill by 86 of the assembly's 106 members on Monday night as "legitimising a perpetuity of power that could threaten democracy".
President Blaise Compaore's ruling Congress for Democracy and Progress introduced the changes arguing that the two-term cap limited the electorate's choice.
But West African political analysts saw the move as a further setback to a tide of democratic reform that swept the region from 1990 with the collapse of Coumminism.

The army has intervened in several countries in the region since then. In some others military rulers simply legitimised their rule through elections in which rivals stood no chance, according to critics.

Compaore himself came to power in the former French colony after a 1987 coup in which his boss, populist leader Captain Thomas Sankara, was killed. Compaore, 45, won presidential elections in 1991 and his first term will end next year when fresh elections are due to take place.

The constitutional changes appeared partly aimed at burying the ghost of Sankara and his revolutionary era. Parliament also voted to modify the words of the national anthem and to change the country's motto, "Fatherland or Death, We Shall Win", which it judged denoted a state of emergency.
The new motto is "Unity, Progress and Justice".
